subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Which subset of canonical readiness conditions, standard and operator hosting profiles, plugin readiness callbacks, activation identity, and release-conformance obligations should OpenClaw accept now?
rationale: The document and linked proof establish feasibility, but only maintainers can choose the permanent core API, availability policy, compatibility boundary, and release support promise.

options.title: Accept the proven foundation
options.body: Approve canonical conditions, compatibility projections, and the proven initial profile/provider surfaces while deferring activation identity and blocking release gates.

options.title: Accept the complete roadmap
options.body: Approve the full RFC, including its unimplemented activation and release-support obligations, as one long-term contract.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Close the proposal if hosting-readiness composition should remain host- or plugin-owned rather than a core support contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the proven foundation
recommendation.body: Approve canonical conditions, compatibility projections, and the proven initial profile/provider surfaces while deferring activation identity and blocking release gates.

likelyOwner.reason: The available implementation review and repository history point to this person as the broadest owner across the affected Gateway, plugin, configuration, and project-direction surfaces.
